# 4-Week Headache Reduction Plan

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/thermometer-half.svg

You’re describing a pattern that often fits **tension-type headaches** or “mixed trigger” headaches from long desk time, short sleep, dehydration, eye strain, stress, and seasonal allergy irritation. The goal for the next month is to lower trigger load and make your day more consistent.

## Likely Triggers and Best-Fit Lifestyle Targets

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/clock.svg

- **Desk posture and muscle tension:** 9 hours seated can tighten the neck, jaw, shoulders, and upper back.
- **Sleep debt:** 6.5 hours on average is often not enough for headache-prone people.
- **Dehydration or irregular meals:** both can make headaches more likely and harder to recover from.
- **Screen strain:** long uninterrupted screen time can trigger eye fatigue and head pressure.
- **Seasonal allergies:** congestion, sinus pressure, poor sleep, and mouth breathing can all contribute.
- **Stress carryover:** even if the workday is “normal,” sustained low-grade stress can build into tension headaches.

## 4-Week Daily Routine and Targets

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/calendar.svg

| Week | Focus | Daily routine | Hydration target | Screen-break target | Ergonomic target |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Baseline + consistency | Wake and sleep at the same time; 5-minute neck/shoulder stretch morning and evening; regular meals | **2.0–2.5 L/day** unless your doctor has told you to limit fluids | **20-20-20** rule plus 5 minutes away from screen each hour | Set chair, monitor, and keyboard to reduce forward head posture |
| 2 | Reduce muscle tension | Add 2 short walk breaks; jaw unclenching check; 5-minute mobility at lunch | **2.2–2.7 L/day** | **5 minutes off-screen every hour**; blink often; reduce glare | Keep elbows near 90°, feet flat, monitor top near eye level |
| 3 | Improve recovery | Aim for an earlier bedtime to reach **7–8 hours**; keep caffeine earlier in the day | **2.2–2.7 L/day** plus extra in hot weather/exercise | Continue hourly breaks; if possible, alternate tasks away from screen | Add lumbar support; keep mouse close to body; avoid cradling phone |
| 4 | Stabilize + personalize | Keep the most effective habits; note patterns from sleep, stress, allergies, and meals | Maintain steady intake; sip through the day, not all at once | Protect breaks during the busiest work periods | Fine-tune chair height, monitor distance, and desk layout |

## Daily Routine That Fits a Desk Job

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg

- **Morning**
  - Drink a glass of water soon after waking.
  - Do 3–5 minutes of neck rolls, shoulder circles, and chest opening.
  - Eat breakfast or at least a protein-containing snack if you tend to skip meals.
- **During work**
  - Use a timer for hourly movement breaks.
  - Every 20 minutes, look 20 feet away for 20 seconds.
  - Keep shoulders relaxed and jaw unclenched.
  - If allergies are active, try to minimize irritants and keep indoor air comfortable.
- **Lunch**
  - Take a 10-minute walk if possible.
  - Step away from the screen completely.
  - Refill water before the afternoon slump.
- **Evening**
  - Reduce late-day screen intensity when possible.
  - Do a short stretch routine for neck, upper back, and chest.
  - Keep caffeine earlier in the day so sleep quality improves.
- **Before bed**
  - Aim for a consistent sleep window.
  - Keep the room dark, cool, and quiet.
  - If congestion is common, use your preferred non-medical comfort measures that help you breathe and sleep better.

## Ergonomic Changes That Usually Help Most

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/laptop.svg

- **Monitor:** top of screen near eye level; screen about an arm’s length away.
- **Chair:** hips slightly above knees; back supported; shoulders relaxed.
- **Keyboard and mouse:** close enough that you do not reach forward.
- **Phone use:** avoid long “head-down” posture; raise the device when possible.
- **Lighting:** reduce glare from windows and overhead lights.
- **Micro-movement:** change position often; even good posture becomes a problem if held too long.

## Red-Flag Symptoms That Need Medical Care

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/exclamation-triangle.svg

Seek medical care promptly if you have any of these:
- A **sudden, severe headache** that peaks quickly or feels like the worst headache of your life
- Headache with **weakness, numbness, confusion, fainting, trouble speaking, or vision loss**
- **Fever, stiff neck, rash**, or severe illness symptoms
- Headache after a **head injury**
- A **new or clearly changing pattern** that is getting worse over time
- Headache with **persistent vomiting** or severe dehydration
- Headache that **wakes you from sleep repeatedly** or is worse when lying down
- Headache with **eye pain**, redness, or major visual changes
- Any headache that feels unusual for you or is not improving with basic self-care
